title: Prayer for Rain and Spiritual Instruction
english: In a fitting time, 'from the end of the earth He brings clouds and makes lightning into rain' (Jeremiah 31:37), as was prophetically announced in Jeremiah. The word, instilling confidence, exhorts one to ask for rain in its proper season; it brought forth: 'The Lord made a vision and a winter rain.' And not once, but many times from above—unless ungodliness having prevailed among the Hebrews has so much disposed them as to make them unworthy of receiving God-sending gifts.

Since, therefore, God always gives drink to the earth for the sake of men, it is proper to seek Him out when drought occurs, and not to pay attention to false divinations, [the text is broken here regarding the toil and labors of those who speak of dreams and deceivers]. This was held [as it was already said concerning Elijah, a servant of God], a single time; for then and then rain occurred. As it is written regarding Jacob, he addressed [us] by letter, saying: 'Elijah, a man with passions like ours (James 5:17), prayed that it might not rain, and it did not rain for three years and six months,' when drought came upon [the land], to which he added: 'The prayer of a righteous man is powerful in its working (James 5:16).'

From these things being done thus, it is necessary to flee always toward God in times of affliction, and not to pay attention to demonic deceptions, the proof of which has been the seeking of God, which will clearly be [seen] with those in royal histories. Sufficiently, as I think, in accordance with the explicit word of Zechariah, one must also attend to the lifting up. Spiritual rain is the God-given teaching, which has been written thus: 'Let the clouds rain down righteousness' (Zechariah 9:6), by which command is given not to give rain when, allegorically speaking, a vineyard is bearing fruit...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: False Prophets and the Wandering Flock
english: "...to us like a preceding and following rain upon the earth." One must understand by thought another preceding rain, which is the word concerning the incarnation of the Savior, and a following one, which is the word concerning his theology. Those who have enjoyed both of these waters say: 'The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, a glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth' (John 1:14). This same understanding is held by that which was written to the Corinthians by Paul: 'Even if we knew Christ according to the flesh, but now we know him no longer' (2 Cor 5:16). To provide the former answer regarding the two covenants, one should use that: 'Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, set apart for the gospel of God, which he foretold through his prophets in the holy Scriptures concerning his Son, the one born of the seed of David according to the flesh, and declared to be the Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness' (Rom 1:3-4).

A third understanding is also stated: let the things 'known and prophesied in part' (1 Cor 13:12) in this present age be taken as a preceding rain, while the 'face to face' seeing which will be shown in the coming age is the following rain. And let these things also be affectionately spoken: let the corrective discipline of morals and appropriate practical virtue be a preceding watering, while the following one is the knowledge of the mysteries of God the Word.

This double rain will exist, God himself providing it, when we proceed toward knowing the Lord through inquiries and the searching of the God-breathed Scriptures and the training appropriate to unhindered contemplation; for when these have been prepared beforehand, the Lord being sought will be found 'ready as the dawn,' becoming a preceding and following rain to the earth that received the seed of Jesus. For in this way the following things will bear fruit, as the spoken word makes manifest what was previously brought forward: resurrection, life, and perfect knowledge, as it says: 'For it will rain upon us like a preceding and following rain upon the earth. And we shall rise and live and stand before him and know' (Hos 6:3).

Having been filled with these God-breathed good things, the one who has sought the Lord as a weary person will release himself from the sayings of false prophets who are more like dreamers than those seeing actual things. Such are those who have launched heresies into Christianity, 'not understanding either what they say or about whom they affirm things' (Acts 17:21).
"attending to the deceptive spirits and teachings of demons, in the hypocrisy of liars, having cauterized their own conscience."

Those who have cast aside watching and sobriety are carried away by false dreams, being swept along by passion, as they sleep and drink at night; for concerning those who are dreaming and always desiring to slumber, it is written: "Those who sleep at night sleep, and at night they drink," being deprived of the light of the truth. Therefore, even if they ever promise a comforting parable, they call out in vain; for no pasture or herb shall come from their supposed divinatory proclamation. Thus they wither like sheep not having pasture, concerning which the holy man said: "The Lord shepherds me, and I shall not want anything; into a place of green pasture, there He has pitched my tent" (Psalm 23:1-2). And this fertile pasture is found by the one entering and exiting the door, other than that of the Savior who declares: "I am the door. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved and will go out and find pasture" (John 10:9).

Being deprived of this, those attending to dreams and false divinations will wither like animals not having feeding-grounds, as they can no longer exist in them being greatly afflicted, the wrath of God being provoked against the faulty shepherds because of their laziness regarding the flock, so that the lambs might be tested by the wrath of God the Shepherd, and the feeding lambs being rebuked and afflicted, just as they themselves will wither along with the gathered sheep.

Indeed, harm has surpassed the flock because of the leaders who fell into ungodliness, about whom God Himself says: "The shepherds were unfaithful to me, and behind useless things they went" (Ezekiel 34:2-10), as they attend to both divination and false dreams being promised, just as the sheep themselves are being harmed, undergoing destruction. For it was most strictly said by Him who tends all: "My people became lost sheep, and their shepherds drove them away," so that the lambs themselves were also afflicted, no longer having the benefit of the feeding pasture. Yet, even if they were thus divided among themselves, through the goodness of the Good Shepherd, the "Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world" was set up for them.

title: The Shepherd and the Warrior
english: Wherein the prophecy says: 'Like a sheep led to slaughter and like a lamb before its shearer being silent' (Isa 53:7), which the Baptist, having more pointedly as a prophet, said: 'Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world' (John 1:29). And once the sin of the world having been removed, the sheep having been benefited no longer have drought or kindred evils, nor the lambs whom the speaker visited: 'And my wrath was provoked against the shepherds' (Zech 11:6).

It is also necessary for us to become under the good chief shepherd, who dwells in the place of green pasture for those being shepherded by him, so that entering and going out, applying ourselves inwardly and outwardly to divine words, we may be experienced in blessedness and eternal life. And the Lord God the Pantokrator, being the one who after being angry heals beneficially those who fell by the indignation, will visit his flock, which happens to be the house of Judah, that is to say, of the one confessing; for Judah is interpreted as confessing. The Lord God Pantokrator, being, visits his own flock; concerning which it is also said in Micah: 'And he will stand and see and will shepherd his flock in strength, the Lord' (Micah 2:12), being Savior. And the Lord God the Pantokrator will visit his flock, the house of Judah, and will array them like his well-ordered horse in war (Zech 10:3). And from him he looked, and from him he arrayed, and from him the bow in wrath; from him will go out everyone departing in the same (Zech 10:4). And they shall be as warriors trampling clay in the roads in war and will be arrayed, because the Lord is with them (Zech 10:5).

That the Lord God Pantokrator is the Only-begotten Son of God, this has been demonstrated previously. For the Trinity being of one substance, the one being begotten being of one substance with the one who begotten, the Savior is Lord God Pantokrator from the Lord God Pantokrator. For how could he not be Lord God, 'who was in the beginning with God' (John 1:1)? And just as 'through him all things came to be' (John 1:3), so also he holds and reigns, as to be for this reason Pantokrator. This, then, is the one being theologized, having arrived to find and save the human race, which having fallen like a sheep from the hundred of the rational [beings], like a best shepherd...

He set his own life as a ransom for which he came to save, as if to oversee his own flock, being the house of Judah, concerning which it is said: 'Judah, your brothers shall praise you' (Ps 105:15). And since a rapid change of progress occurs for those being benefited, he arranges those completing his flock, like a fine horse, 'all having been equipped with one mind and one purpose,' as if to become a best charioteer from a shepherd, riding salvationally.

This good has increased by having sent an embassy of those having longing for his arrival, saying: 'Mount the horses, and your riding shall be salvation' (Ps 44:3). From the house of Judah, from a flock having become a fine horse, he looked out and arranged from it a bow, from which he sends arrows, words concerning punishment and threat; concerning which he who arranged the bow said: 'I will satiate my arrows with blood' (Ps 18:14), and again: 'My arrows will complete them.' It was also said previously that punishments are called arrows for some profound reason. In the seventh Psalm, indeed, concerning the judge of all, living and dead, it is said: 'He has bent his bow and prepared it, and in it he has prepared instruments of death; he has worked his arrows for those being burned' (Ps 7:12-13).

What then will happen when the Lord God the Pantokrator looks out from Judah and arranges from it a war-bow, or when those having suffered well by him from the [people] of Judah become experienced warriors of war? He will go out in the same manner, the one going out prepared for war, so that to tread the mud of roads, many falling, as mud shall become from the blood. And this happens to those conquering, but not to those being defeated. For those having turned to flight are pursued and hasten, but those charging and hastening, showing their knees through fear, tread the mud of the blood of the slaughtered, returning like the one going out on horseback.

When these [righteous] ones exist, the Lord their God will be fighting for them and about them, as to say graciously: 'The Lord of strengths is with us, a defender is our God Jacob' (Ps 46:7), and again: 'In God we will do strength, and he will bring to nothing those crushing us' (Ps 46:10).'
